structure.title: Testing a disputed death
structure.text: Early encounters make the court's appearances and testimony uncertain, prompting attempts to establish what happened.

structure.title: The effects of investigation
structure.text: Later acts widen the consequences of those attempts. Soliloquies expose thoughts unavailable to the other characters.

people.name: Hamlet
people.text: A student prince called home from university for his father's funeral, who finds his mother already remarried and his own place at court changed.

people.name: Claudius
people.text: The dead king's brother, now on the throne and married to the queen, a capable ruler who wants Hamlet to stop mourning.

people.name: Gertrude
people.text: Hamlet's mother, who married her late husband's brother within two months, and who is caught between her son and her new king.

context.title: A royal household
context.text: Marriage and succession shape the state as well as the family. Private grief becomes a public problem when its owner is a potential ruler.

context.title: Revenge drama
context.text: A demand for vengeance sets a task, but does not establish reliable evidence or moral permission. The play keeps those questions unsettled.
context.takeaway: The command is not the same as justification.

notice.text: Track listeners, hidden observers, and reports.
notice.why: A conversation may serve purposes its participants do not share.

notice.text: Compare Hamlet's self-accusations with his actions.
notice.why: His account of himself is part of the drama rather than a neutral assessment.

opening: Hamlet's father is dead, his mother has married his uncle, and everyone would like him to stop making things uncomfortable. Then a ghost tells him the death was murder. Revenge sounds straightforward until Hamlet has to establish what happened, decide whom he can trust, and become someone capable of carrying it out. Meanwhile the court watches him think. Shakespeare gives him enough wit to make almost anyone look foolish and enough doubt to turn every possible action into another reason to hesitate.
